category: Geometry & Regions II: Special Regions, Polygons, Polyhedra, Mesh Annotations & Region Predicates
description: Additional geometric regions (half-lines, half-spaces, conic hulls, stadium and capsule shapes, tori, named polyhedra), polygon and polyhedron analysis and decomposition, region relations and predicates (equality, containment, disjointness, boundedness, convexity), Minkowski dilation/erosion, region fitting, moments and inertia, angles, coordinate bounds, mesh-cell annotations and quality control.

tools.name: HalfLine
tools.description: Infinite linear regions usable as graphics primitives and in region computations: HalfLine (ray from p through q or in direction v), InfiniteLine (listed), HalfPlane, InfinitePlane (listed), HalfSpace (points with normal.x <= c), Hyperplane and AffineSpace, plus ConicHullRegion for cones/wedges. Use them for clipping, visibility and unbounded constraint regions.
tools.usage:
HalfLine[{p1, p2}]
HalfLine[p, v]
HalfPlane[{p1, p2}, w]
HalfPlane[p, v, w]
HalfSpace[n, p]
HalfSpace[n, c]
Hyperplane[n, p]
AffineSpace[p, {v1, v2, ...}]
ConicHullRegion[p, {v1, v2, ...}]
tools.example:
RegionMember[HalfSpace[{0, 1}, 0], {1, -3}] (* True: y <= 0 *)
RegionIntersection[Disk[], HalfPlane[{0, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, 1}]] // Region
Graphics[{HalfLine[{0, 0}, {1, 1}], Circle[]}, PlotRange -> 2]

tools.name: StadiumShape
tools.description: StadiumShape (2D: segment swept by a disk) and CapsuleShape (3D: segment swept by a ball) are the exact Minkowski-sum shapes used for thick lines, collision bounds and slot geometry; both work as graphics primitives and regions (RegionMember, Area/Volume, DiscretizeRegion). FilledTorus and Torus give solid/surface tori.
tools.usage:
StadiumShape[{{x1, y1}, {x2, y2}}, r]
CapsuleShape[{{x1, y1, z1}, {x2, y2, z2}}, r]
FilledTorus[{x, y, z}, {rinner, router}]
Torus[{x, y, z}, {rinner, router}]

parameters.name: {rinner, router}
parameters.description: Tube and ring radii of the torus.

tools.example:
Area[StadiumShape[{{0, 0}, {4, 0}}, 1]] (* 8 + Pi *)
Graphics3D[{Opacity[0.6], CapsuleShape[{{0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 3}}, 1], FilledTorus[{4, 0, 0}, {0.5, 2}]}]
RegionMember[CapsuleShape[{{0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 3}}, 1], {0.5, 0, 1.5}] (* True *)

tools.name: Cube
tools.description: Named regular polyhedra as regions and graphics primitives: Cube, Tetrahedron, Octahedron, Dodecahedron, Icosahedron (all with optional edge length, centre and orientation), plus Hexahedron (general 8-vertex solid), Pyramid and Prism; Polyhedron builds an arbitrary polyhedron from faces and PolyhedronData supplies hundreds of named ones. All support Volume, RegionMember, DiscretizeRegion and Boolean operations.
tools.usage:
Cube[]
Cube[l]
Cube[{x, y, z}, l]
Tetrahedron[]
Dodecahedron[{x, y, z}, l]
Hexahedron[{p1, ..., p8}]
Pyramid[{p1, p2, p3, p4, p5}]
Prism[{p1, ..., p6}]
Polyhedron[{f1, f2, ...}]
Polyhedron[{p1, ..., pn}, {{i1, i2, ...}, ...}]

parameters.name: {f1, ...}
parameters.description: Faces as coordinate lists, or vertex list plus face index lists.

tools.example:
Volume[Dodecahedron[]] // N
Graphics3D[{Opacity[0.5], Cube[], Red, Icosahedron[{2, 0, 0}, 0.8]}]
RegionMember[Tetrahedron[], {0.1, 0.1, 0.1}]
Polyhedron[{{0, 0, 0}, {1, 0, 0}, {0, 1, 0}, {0, 0, 1}}, {{1, 3, 2}, {1, 2, 4}, {1, 4, 3}, {2, 3, 4}}] // Volume

tools.name: PolyhedronCoordinates
tools.description: Polyhedron analysis: PolyhedronCoordinates (vertex coordinates), PolyhedronAngle (dihedral angles at edges), DualPolyhedron, CanonicalizePolyhedron (canonical face/vertex form), ConvexPolyhedronQ, SimplePolyhedronQ, PolyhedronDecomposition (into tetrahedra/convex pieces), OuterPolyhedron/InnerPolyhedron for polyhedra with voids, and RandomPolyhedron. Use them to validate and process imported solids before meshing or printing.
tools.usage:
PolyhedronCoordinates[poly]
PolyhedronAngle[poly, e]
DualPolyhedron[poly]
CanonicalizePolyhedron[poly]
ConvexPolyhedronQ[poly]
SimplePolyhedronQ[poly]
PolyhedronDecomposition[poly]
RandomPolyhedron[{"ConvexHull", n}]

parameters.name: e
parameters.description: Edge as a pair of points.

tools.example:
DualPolyhedron[Cube[]] (* an Octahedron *)
PolyhedronDecomposition[Dodecahedron[]] // Length
ConvexPolyhedronQ[PolyhedronData["GreatDodecahedron", "Polyhedron"]] (* False *)

tools.name: PolygonDecomposition
tools.description: Decomposes a (possibly non-convex, multi-component or holed) polygon into simple, convex or triangular pieces; SimplePolygonQ, ConvexPolygonQ, PolygonCoordinates, PolygonAngle (interior/exterior angles), CanonicalizePolygon, CrossingPolygon (self-intersecting polygon semantics), OuterPolygon / InnerPolygon (boundary and holes) and RandomPolygon complete the polygon toolkit. Used for rendering, area computations and CAM path generation.
tools.usage:
PolygonDecomposition[poly]
PolygonDecomposition[poly, "Convex"]
PolygonDecomposition[poly, "Triangle"]
SimplePolygonQ[poly]
ConvexPolygonQ[poly]
PolygonAngle[poly]
PolygonAngle[poly, p]
CanonicalizePolygon[poly]
OuterPolygon[poly]
InnerPolygon[poly]
RandomPolygon[n]

parameters.name: poly
parameters.description: Polygon (with holes given as Polygon[{outer, hole1, ...}] or Polygon[outer -> holes]).

tools.example:
star = RegularPolygon[{5, 2}] // Polygon@PolygonCoordinates@# &;
PolygonDecomposition[Polygon[{{0, 0}, {2, 0}, {2, 2}, {1, 1}, {0, 2}}], "Convex"]
PolygonAngle[Triangle[{{0, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, 1}}]] (* {Pi/2, Pi/4, Pi/4} *)
ConvexPolygonQ[RandomPolygon[8]]

tools.name: RegionEqual
tools.description: Region relations: RegionEqual (same point set), RegionWithin[reg1, reg2] (reg2 contained in reg1), RegionDisjoint (no common points). They work symbolically on exact regions (Disk, Polygon, ImplicitRegion) and numerically on meshes, and are the basis of collision and containment checks.
tools.usage:
RegionEqual[reg1, reg2]
RegionWithin[reg1, reg2]
RegionDisjoint[reg1, reg2]

parameters.name: reg1, reg2
parameters.description: Regions of the same embedding dimension.

tools.example:
RegionWithin[Disk[{0, 0}, 2], Rectangle[{-1, -1}, {1, 1}]] (* True *)
RegionDisjoint[Ball[{0, 0, 0}, 1], Ball[{3, 0, 0}, 1]] (* True *)
RegionEqual[RegionUnion[Disk[], Disk[]], Disk[]] (* True *)

tools.name: BoundedRegionQ
tools.description: Region predicates: BoundedRegionQ (fits in a finite box), ConvexRegionQ, SolidRegionQ (full-dimensional in its embedding space), RegionEmbeddingDimension (dimension of the ambient space, versus RegionDimension of the region itself) and ConstantRegionQ (no symbolic parameters). Use them to choose algorithms and validate user-supplied regions.
tools.usage:
BoundedRegionQ[reg]
ConvexRegionQ[reg]
SolidRegionQ[reg]
RegionEmbeddingDimension[reg]
ConstantRegionQ[reg]
tools.example:
BoundedRegionQ[HalfPlane[{0, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, 1}]] (* False *)
ConvexRegionQ[Annulus[]] (* False *)
{RegionDimension[Circle[]], RegionEmbeddingDimension[Circle[]]} (* {1, 2} *)
SolidRegionQ[Sphere[]] (* False *) ; SolidRegionQ[Ball[]] (* True *)

tools.name: RegionDilation
tools.description: RegionDilation[reg, r] is the Minkowski sum of a region with a disk/ball of radius r (offsetting outward), RegionDilation[reg1, reg2] the general Minkowski sum, and RegionErosion the Minkowski difference (offset inward). Used for tolerance zones, tool-path offsets, configuration-space obstacles and rounding corners. Introduced in 12.3.
tools.usage:
RegionDilation[reg, r]
RegionDilation[reg1, reg2]
RegionErosion[reg, r]
RegionErosion[reg1, reg2]
tools.example:
sq = Rectangle[{0, 0}, {2, 2}];
Region[RegionDilation[sq, 0.3]] (* rounded square *)
Area[RegionErosion[sq, 0.5]] (* 1 *)
RegionDilation[Triangle[], Rectangle[{0, 0}, {0.2, 0.2}]]

tools.name: RegionFit
tools.description: Fits a geometric model ("Line", "Plane", "Circle", "Sphere", "Cylinder", "Cone", ...) to a point cloud robustly (RANSAC-style, ignoring outliers), returning the region or properties such as inlier points; ConcaveHullMesh and GradientFittedMesh reconstruct surfaces from points. Use it for LiDAR / scan processing and shape detection. Introduced in 13.0.
tools.usage:
RegionFit[{p1, p2, ...}, "model"]
RegionFit[pts, "model", "prop"]
ConcaveHullMesh[pts]
ConcaveHullMesh[pts, alpha]

tools.name: RegionMoment
tools.description: RegionMoment integrates monomials x^i y^j z^k over a region (raw polynomial moments), and MomentOfInertia gives the moment of inertia about an axis or the full inertia matrix about a point or the centroid, assuming unit density. With RegionCentroid, Area and Volume they provide the standard mass properties of CAD solids.
tools.usage:
RegionMoment[reg, {i, j, ...}]
MomentOfInertia[reg]
MomentOfInertia[reg, pt]
MomentOfInertia[reg, pt, v]
tools.example:
RegionMoment[Disk[], {2, 0}] (* Pi/4 *)
MomentOfInertia[Cuboid[{0, 0, 0}, {a, b, c}]] // Simplify (* inertia tensor about the centroid *)
MomentOfInertia[Cylinder[{{0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, h}}, r], {0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 1}] (* Pi h r^4/2 *)

tools.name: PlanarAngle
tools.description: Geometric angle measures: PlanarAngle (angle at a vertex between two half-lines or of a triangle), DihedralAngle (between two half-planes / faces), SolidAngle (subtended by vectors or a region from a point), PolygonAngle and PolyhedronAngle (interior angles of polygons/polyhedra), with VectorAngle for plain vectors and AngleBisector for constructions. They return exact results for exact input.
tools.usage:
PlanarAngle[p -> {q1, q2}]
PlanarAngle[{q1, p, q2}]
PlanarAngle[..., "Interior" | "Reflex" | "Counterclockwise"]
DihedralAngle[{p1, p2} -> {q1, q2}]
SolidAngle[p, {v1, v2, v3}]
SolidAngle[p, reg]
AngleBisector[{q1, p, q2}]

tools.name: CollinearPoints
tools.description: Point-configuration predicates: CollinearPoints (all on one line), CoplanarPoints (all on one plane), PositivelyOrientedPoints / NegativelyOrientedPoints (orientation of a simplex, i.e. the sign of the signed volume), plus Circumsphere / Insphere and CircleThrough for circumscribed and inscribed spheres/circles. Exact for exact coordinates and tolerant for approximate ones.
tools.usage:
CollinearPoints[{p1, p2, p3, ...}]
CoplanarPoints[{p1, p2, p3, p4, ...}]
PositivelyOrientedPoints[{p1, ..., pn+1}]
Circumsphere[{p1, ..., pn+1}]
Insphere[{p1, ..., pn+1}]
CircleThrough[{p1, p2, p3}]
tools.example:
CollinearPoints[{{0, 0}, {1, 1}, {2, 2}}] (* True *)
Circumsphere[{{0, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, 1}}] (* Sphere[{1/2, 1/2}, 1/Sqrt[2]] *)
Insphere[Tetrahedron[]]
PositivelyOrientedPoints[{{0, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, 1}}] (* True: counterclockwise *)

tools.name: CoordinateBounds
tools.description: CoordinateBounds gives {{xmin, xmax}, {ymin, ymax}, ...} of a point set (with optional padding), CoordinateBoundingBox the two corner points, CoordinateBoundsArray a grid of points spanning bounds (for sampling), and BoundingRegion the smallest region of a given type ("MinDisk", "MinBall", "MinRectangle", "MinOrientedCuboid", "FastEllipsoid", ...) enclosing points. Used for plot ranges, spatial indexing and collision bounds.
tools.usage:
CoordinateBounds[pts]
CoordinateBounds[pts, delta]
CoordinateBoundingBox[pts]
CoordinateBoundsArray[{{xmin, xmax}, {ymin, ymax}}, dx]
BoundingRegion[pts]
BoundingRegion[pts, "MinDisk"]
BoundingRegion[reg, "MinOrientedCuboid"]

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: List of points (or a region for BoundingRegion).

tools.example:
pts = RandomReal[{-1, 1}, {100, 2}];
CoordinateBounds[pts, Scaled[0.1]]
BoundingRegion[pts, "MinDisk"]
CoordinateBoundsArray[{{0, 1}, {0, 1}}, 0.25] // Flatten[#, 1] &

tools.name: MeshCellMeasure
tools.description: Per-cell annotations of MeshRegion/BoundaryMeshRegion read via AnnotationValue or PropertyValue: MeshCellMeasure (length/area/volume of each cell), MeshCellCentroid, MeshCellQuality (shape quality in [0, 1]), MeshCellIndex, MeshCellMarker (integer markers from ToElementMesh) and MeshCellLabel / MeshCellStyle / MeshCellHighlight for display. Use them to inspect mesh quality, weight computations per element and select cells by marker.
tools.usage:
AnnotationValue[{mesh, {d, All}}, MeshCellMeasure]
PropertyValue[{mesh, {2, All}}, MeshCellQuality]
AnnotationValue[{mesh, {2, All}}, MeshCellCentroid]
MeshRegion[mesh, MeshCellStyle -> {{2, 1} -> Red}, MeshCellLabel -> {0 -> "Index"}]
HighlightMesh[mesh, {2, i}]

parameters.name: {d, All}
parameters.description: Cell specification: dimension d and index (All for every cell).

tools.name: MeshQualityGoal
tools.description: Options controlling discretization: MeshQualityGoal (0 to 1, or "Minimal"/"Maximal") for element shape quality, MaxCellMeasure (maximum cell size, per dimension or as "Length"/"Area"/"Volume"), MeshRefinementFunction (custom refinement predicate), AccuracyGoal/PrecisionGoal for boundary fidelity and MeshCellHighlight for display. Used by DiscretizeRegion, DiscretizeGraphics, BoundaryDiscretizeRegion, ToElementMesh and NDSolve's finite-element method.
tools.usage:
DiscretizeRegion[reg, MaxCellMeasure -> {"Area" -> 0.01}, MeshQualityGoal -> 0.9]
DiscretizeRegion[reg, MeshRefinementFunction -> Function[{vertices, area}, area > 0.001 && Norm[Mean[vertices]] < 0.5]]
ToElementMesh[reg, "MaxCellMeasure" -> 0.001, "MeshOrder" -> 2]

parameters.name: MaxCellMeasure
parameters.description: Number or rules per measure type.

parameters.name: MeshQualityGoal
parameters.description: Target quality; higher is slower but better conditioned.

parameters.name: MeshRefinementFunction
parameters.description: Function of (cell vertices, cell measure) returning True to refine.

tools.name: FindMeshDefects
tools.description: Detects defects in a surface mesh ("FlippedFaces", "HoleEdges", "IsolatedVertices", "TinyFaces", "TinyComponents", "TJunctionEdges", "OverlappingFaces", ...), returning the offending cells or a highlighted mesh, complementing RepairMesh (listed) for preparing scans and CAD exports for 3D printing or simulation. Introduced in 12.0.
tools.usage:
FindMeshDefects[mesh]
FindMeshDefects[mesh, "defect"]
FindMeshDefects[mesh, {"defect1", "defect2"}, "Cells"]
FindMeshDefects[mesh, All, "Count"]

tools.name: HighlightMesh
tools.description: Highlights specified cells (by dimension and index, or all cells of a dimension) of a mesh region for visual inspection, the mesh analogue of HighlightGraph; MeshCellStyle and MeshCellHighlight options give persistent styling. Useful to show boundary conditions, marked sub-domains or poor-quality elements.
tools.usage:
HighlightMesh[mesh, {d, i}]
HighlightMesh[mesh, {{d1, i1}, {d2, i2}, ...}]
HighlightMesh[mesh, Style[{d, i}, Red]]
HighlightMesh[mesh, {1, All}]

parameters.name: {d, i}
parameters.description: Cell dimension and index (All for every cell of that dimension).

tools.example:
mesh = DiscretizeRegion[Rectangle[], MaxCellMeasure -> 0.05];
HighlightMesh[mesh, {Style[{1, All}, Gray], Style[{2, 1}, Red]}]

tools.name: ArrayMesh
tools.description: Converts a 2D or 3D array of cell values into a MeshRegion of unit squares/cubes (only cells with value 1, or matching a specified value, are included), turning pixel/voxel masks into geometry for Area/Volume, Boolean operations, NDSolve domains and 3D printing; ImageMesh (listed) does the same directly from images.
tools.usage:
ArrayMesh[array]
ArrayMesh[array, v]
ArrayMesh[array, {v1, v2, ...}]
ArrayMesh[array, DataRange -> {{xmin, xmax}, {ymin, ymax}}]

tools.name: BooleanRegion
tools.description: Applies an arbitrary Boolean combination (given as a function of membership predicates) to regions, generalizing RegionUnion/Intersection/Difference/SymmetricDifference; CSGRegion (13.0+) builds constructive solid geometry trees with "Union", "Intersection", "Difference" that render fast and can be discretized or queried, and CSGRegionTree shows the tree. RegionSymmetricDifference is the XOR case.
tools.usage:
BooleanRegion[f, {reg1, reg2, ...}]
BooleanRegion[Xor, {reg1, reg2}]
RegionSymmetricDifference[reg1, reg2]
CSGRegion["Union", {reg1, reg2}]
CSGRegion["Difference", {reg1, reg2}]
CSGRegionTree[csg]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Boolean function of the membership values, e.g. #1 && !#2 &.

tools.name: CanonicalizeRegion
tools.description: Converts a region to a canonical representation (e.g. simplifying nested unions, removing degenerate pieces, choosing standard primitive forms), and RegionConvert converts between representations ("Implicit", "Parametric", "Polygon", "Polyhedron"). Use them to normalise regions before comparison (RegionEqual) or export.
tools.usage:
CanonicalizeRegion[reg]
RegionConvert[reg, "Implicit"]
RegionConvert[reg, "Parametric"]
tools.example:
RegionConvert[Disk[{1, 2}, 3], "Implicit"] (* ImplicitRegion[(x-1)^2 + (y-2)^2 <= 9, {x, y}] *)
RegionConvert[Sphere[], "Parametric"]
CanonicalizeRegion[RegionUnion[Disk[], Disk[]]]

tools.name: ShellRegion
tools.description: ShellRegion[reg, t] gives the thin shell of thickness t inside the boundary of a solid region (a hollow version), and SubdivisionRegion applies subdivision surfaces (Catmull-Clark/Loop) to polygonal meshes for smoothing. Both are 13.x additions relevant to 3D printing and modelling.
tools.usage:
ShellRegion[reg]
ShellRegion[reg, t]
SubdivisionRegion[reg]
SubdivisionRegion[reg, n]
tools.example:
Volume[ShellRegion[Ball[], 0.1]] // N
SubdivisionRegion[DiscretizeGraphics[Cube[]], 3]

tools.name: Region
tools.description: Region[reg] wraps any region so that it displays graphically with automatic styling (the quickest way to look at an ImplicitRegion, mesh or Boolean combination), and accepts graphics options; it is also used by RegionPlot-style displays and inside Graphics via Region[reg] as a primitive-like object. Not needed for computation, only for visualisation.
tools.usage:
Region[reg]
Region[reg, opts]
Region[Style[reg, Red]]
tools.example:
Region[ImplicitRegion[x^2 + y^3 <= 1 && y > -1, {x, y}]]
Region[Style[RegionDifference[Ball[], Cuboid[]], Opacity[0.5], Orange], Axes -> True]

tools.name: ArcCurvature
tools.description: Differential geometry of curves: ArcCurvature (curvature of a parametric curve), FrenetSerretSystem (curvature, torsion and the tangent/normal/binormal frame), plus the coordinate-system helpers ToPolarCoordinates / FromPolarCoordinates and ToSphericalCoordinates / FromSphericalCoordinates. Useful for path planning, robotics and analysing spirals and space curves.
tools.usage:
ArcCurvature[{x[t], y[t]}, t]
ArcCurvature[{x[t], y[t], z[t]}, t]
FrenetSerretSystem[{x[t], y[t], z[t]}, t]
ToPolarCoordinates[{x, y}]
FromSphericalCoordinates[{r, theta, phi}]
tools.example:
ArcCurvature[{Cos[t], Sin[t]}, t] (* 1 *)
{{kappa, tau}, frame} = FrenetSerretSystem[{Cos[t], Sin[t], t}, t]; Simplify[{kappa, tau}] (* {1/2, 1/2} *)
ToPolarCoordinates[{1, 1}] (* {Sqrt[2], Pi/4} *)

tools.name: GeometricAssertion
tools.description: GeometricAssertion states constraints on the objects of a GeometricScene ("Concyclic", "Collinear", "Parallel", "Perpendicular", "Congruent", "Regular", "Convex", "Tangent", ...); RandomInstance then produces concrete coordinates satisfying the scene and FindGeometricConjectures discovers further relations. The classical construction helpers Midpoint, AngleBisector, PerpendicularBisector, CircleThrough, TriangleCenter, TriangleMeasurement and TriangleConstruct complete the synthetic-geometry toolkit.
tools.usage:
GeometricScene[{a, b, c}, {Triangle[{a, b, c}], GeometricAssertion[{a, b, c}, "Regular"]}]
RandomInstance[scene]
Midpoint[{p, q}]
PerpendicularBisector[{p, q}]
TriangleCenter[tri, "Circumcenter"]
TriangleMeasurement[tri, "Inradius"]
TriangleConstruct[tri, "Incircle"]
tools.example:
tri = Triangle[{{0, 0}, {4, 0}, {1, 3}}];
TriangleCenter[tri, "Circumcenter"]
TriangleMeasurement[tri, "Area"]
RandomInstance[GeometricScene[{a, b, c, d}, {Polygon[{a, b, c, d}], GeometricAssertion[{a, b, c, d}, "Concyclic"]}]]
